scope: Nine common locator matchers reuse the pinned predicate semantics through the independent native assertion path. Class arrays, CSS before/after pseudo-elements, multiple selected values, exact roles and accessible text support their tested defaults, negation, configured/per-call timeouts and runner reporting.

The private asynchronous context observer waits for enrollment before publication, preserves the originating scope through late allocation and closure, rejects recursive lifecycle operations and releases retired observer references.

The private action observer associates admitted trace calls with pinned runner step IDs. Expect wrappers own matcher completion; mapped locations, safe previews, original completion ownership and pinned trace-model parent/clock merging pass controlled checks on Bun and Node22/24.

Manual assertion traces retain top-level predicate options and exact failed-negation metadata even when diagnostic text is truncated. Paired real runner archives pass on headless shell and full Chrome.

Packed alias ESM/CommonJS consumers pass the shared matcher corpus on both browser builds. Combined manual snapshots, network resources, filmstrips, source files and runner screenshots also pass on full Chrome.
retainedFailures: The first full attempt passed 71 groups, then failed guardian cleanup and renderer-close deadlines in the lifecycle module. An unchanged seven-case lifecycle rerun also missed guardian deadlines. All observed owned processes eventually exited.

The second full attempt passed 34 groups, then an unchanged one-second request-order probe expired before the fixture driver accepted it. The outer watchdog observed a scheduling gap near three seconds while the shared host was heavily loaded. No owned processes remained.

Current and previous-checkpoint drivers each passed two controlled guardian comparisons. A later seven-case lifecycle run passed with existing ownership diagnostics enabled and unchanged deadlines. These observations support contention as a possibility; they do not establish the exact cause of every earlier failure.

Two initial peer reference-fixture attempts were corrected: a synchronous validation throw needed an async wrapper, and page-close assertion rejection text differed from the expected substring. Both attempts remain retained.
limitations: This is focused development acceptance, not a complete 112-group core pass. The previous 104-group full checkpoint and later public snapshot follow-up keep their original scope and binary identities.
Automatic runner trace policies remain rejected. The private boundaries do not establish final runner archive assembly, aggregate resource limits, retention policies or automatic viewer acceptance.
toHaveJSProperty, toBeInViewport, screenshot/ARIA snapshot assertions and other unimplemented matchers remain unsupported. The production cache eligibility whitelist is unchanged.
No new performance measurement, native Linux result or release support claim.

The custom toHaveRole declaration currently accepts string, broader than the pinned role literal union. Positive consumer type checks do not establish identical role-type rejection or runtime coverage of every ARIA role.
